newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Three Swedish Riksbank members urge early EMU link.
newsitem.headline: Three Swedish Riksbank members urge early EMU link.

text.p: Three board members of Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Tuesday that Sweden should not wait to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) but should be among the first round to join.

Chairman Kjell-Olof Feldt, vice Chairman Bengt Westerberg and board member Johan Gernandt reiterated the opinion expressed earlier by the Riksbank, dismissing a wait-and-see recommendation by an official government commission.
"Our conclusion is that the Calmfors commission's arguments for waiting with EMU membership do not stand up when scrutinised," the trio said in a column in Swedish daily newspaper Svenska Dagbladet.

The Calmfors commission, set up by the minority Social Democrats government and headed by Lars Calmfors, looked at possible Swedish EMU membership and concluded that Sweden should wait to see how it develops before joining.
But Feldt, Westerberg and Gernandt were against the commission's views that Sweden should wait until unemployment was lower and the labour market functioned better.
"There is no reason to believe that the possibilities to fight unemployment would be better if we choose to remain outside (EMU)," they said.

"But we do not want to argue that the membership per se will solve our employment problems. To handle these problems requires a range of measures spanning a broad field, where wage development is a key factor.
"We have an impression that labour market participants, after all the debate and after experiences from the past decades have, at least in principle, realised that."
The three argued that Sweden should be among the first wave of countries to join the monetary union on January 1, 1999.

"It is evident that the countries -- even if they meet convergence criteria -- that choose to stand aside will have less influence in these issues than those that want to join and do join from the start," they said.
